| [THEORY-017](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-017.md) v7 | Hilbert-space parts are extra data, not intrinsic | Carroll (2021), [LIT-123](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-123.md): a quantum theory is fixed up to unitary equivalence by the Hamiltonian's spectrum, and subsystems come from a factorisation that the dynamics must select. Van Rijsbergen ([LIT-262](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-262.md)) computes only traces and inner products, and treats each observable's eigenbasis as a "point of view". DisCoCat's ε/η composition ([LIT-273](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-273.md)) is orthogonally covariant, while its Frobenius sequel ([LIT-272](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-272.md)) stipulates a basis and composes by elementwise product in it. [THEORY-004](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-004.md) is the same point for learned representations. This is a synthesis across the four, not a result any one of them states. It does not say that basis-dependent models are wrong; it says what they have assumed. | Active |
| [THEORY-043](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-043.md) v6 | Nested-agent minds split on unprincipled criteria | Minsky's society of mind builds a mind downward, out of agents that are not minds. Schwitzgebel ([LIT-159](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-159.md)) builds a candidate mind upward, out of agents that are. The readings agree that agency survives both directions: Block grants a homunculi-head beliefs, List grants organised groups agency and awareness, Levin finds nested goal-pursuing collectives (his "Selves") at every scale. The dispute narrows to phenomenal consciousness, and every published way to accept the downward move while refusing the upward one is either an anti-nesting principle (Putnam's stipulation, IIT's exclusion postulate, Kammerer's functional version), each introduced for or justified weakly by the verdict it gives, or an architectural criterion that would count against a loosely coupled society of mind as much as against a nation. Proposed: an account of where a dispute stands, from philosophical argument and no measurement. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-232](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-232.md) v2 | Agency grows when parts resolve constraints | Watson (2023), [LIT-990](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-990.md), read in full in [NOTE-747](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-747.md). A perspective essay's definition, argued and illustrated, not proved: agency of a whole with respect to its parts is the reduction in the parts' total frustration at equilibrium that its organization achieves over the old one, shown by directed uphill excursions to lower minima. It is comparative and sets no threshold for an additional agent, and it holds only relative to a stipulated decomposition and stipulated goals for the parts. That bottom-up learning produces such organization is reported from earlier models, not shown here. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-443](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-443.md) | Biological individuals needn't be organisms | Wilson and Barker (SEP, 2007; substantive revision 2024), [LIT-168](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-168.md), read in [NOTE-114](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-114.md). That organisms are not the only biological individuals is argued from examples; that evolutionary and physiological individuality is the most recognised distinction is a survey judgement. The nine-region framework that places each case is the authors' own and tentative, and its figures draw as disjoint the categories the text says overlap. It offers no criterion of parthood and leaves holobionts open. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-448](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-448.md) | Pregnancy defeats a consistent substance count | Meincke (2021), [LIT-142](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-142.md), read in [NOTE-115](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-115.md). The critique of the Parthood View under substance ontology holds on its own and is the paper's firm contribution. The positive view rests on five process-biology premises assumed for the sake of argument, and is programmatic by the paper's own word; "something in between one and two" has no formal content. It keeps parthood rather than rejecting it, and it draws no ethical conclusion. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-452](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-452.md) | Supervaluation and near-identity count one cat | Lewis (1993), [LIT-1015](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1015.md), read in full in [NOTE-722](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-722.md). Two answers to Unger's problem of the many, offered together. Supervaluation makes "there is one cat" super-true at the granted cost that nothing is super-truly the cat. Almost-identity, which is overlap and not similarity, makes the many candidates "almost one". It is not transitive and its threshold is left undecided. Each covers a case the other fails: Fred's house needs supervaluation, and supervaluation is natural only where the candidates differ little. It assumes semantic indecision, perdurance and no natural joint among the candidates. It has no metric, no dynamics and no threshold, so it is a precedent for counting by something weaker than identity, not evidence for any of the record's claims. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-476](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-476.md) | Stage-aggregate persons make identity matter | Lewis (1976), [LIT-446](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-446.md), read in [NOTE-373](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-373.md). Shown: that identity being one-one and all-or-nothing, and what matters branching and coming in degrees, do not entail that identity is not what matters, once stages and continuants are told apart; and that under supervaluation degrees of I-relatedness equal degrees of R-relatedness. Stipulated: that persons are the maximal R-interrelated aggregates. Conceded as costly: counting persons by tensed identity, which "is not a kind of identity". | Proposed |
| [THEORY-493](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-493.md) | Three axiom pairings yield GEM; Simons' doesn't | Varzi, SEP "Mereology" (2003, revised June 2026), [LIT-124](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-124.md), read in full in [NOTE-163](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-163.md). A result the entry reports with citations (Hovda 2009; Cotnoir and Varzi 2019) and a countermodel (its Fig. 4; Pietruszczak 2000a, Pontow 2004), and which corrects Simons (1987), Casati and Varzi (1999) and the entry's own 2003 edition. The record has not checked the proofs. It is stated for first-order theories with a single primitive P and infinitary principles as axiom schemas, and it is a fact about axiom systems: it does not say classical mereology is true of anything. | Active |
| [THEORY-507](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-507.md) v2 | Functional isomorphs share experiences | Chalmers (1995), [LIT-392](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-392.md), read in full in [NOTE-347](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-347.md), with the one-page sketch in "Facing Up", [LIT-406](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-406.md) ([NOTE-336](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-336.md)). A plausibility argument by the author's own account: the fading- and dancing-qualia conditionals are strong given the replacement series; their rejection rests on a premise about self-knowledge drawn from familiar cases. It extends to a population of people implementing a person's neurons, so it rules out absolute anti-nesting for isomorphs. It does not reach any system that is not an isomorph of something conscious, which includes every actual AI system and every group. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-512](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-512.md) | Extended mind can reach belief, not consciousness | Chalmers (2019), [LIT-415](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-415.md), read in [NOTE-356](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-356.md), and his foreword to Clark's book (2008), [LIT-421](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-421.md), read in [NOTE-369](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-369.md). The 1998 thesis is satisfied by wired-in "extended circuits" that its critics accept, so the controversial thesis is constitution through perception and action. The perception-action boundary is then the strongest objection, met by revisionism, not refuted. Consciousness does not extend this way, on an imported criterion (direct availability, "not mediated by other mental states") and on the absence of any working twin case. Both halves are proposals defended against a few cases; the criterion is the author's earlier correlate of consciousness, not an argument made here. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-514](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-514.md) | Constraint closure doesn't single out organisms | Baedke (2025), [LIT-167](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-167.md), read in full in [NOTE-148](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-148.md). The negative half, that persister criteria are too permissive, is argued from the literature: closure has been applied to symbioses, ecosystems and eusocial colonies, and Mossio (2024) concedes that "organized systems are not necessarily organisms". The positive half, the overcomer, is drawn "with rough brushstrokes" (p. 51) from three cases, two of which are lineage-level evolution or colony-triggered plasticity, and its uniqueness to organisms is asserted, with the one contrast (colony against ant) presupposing its verdict. Proposed. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-528](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-528.md) | Embedded cognition explains extended cases | Rupert (2004), [LIT-422](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-422.md), read in [NOTE-343](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-343.md). The past-endorsement dilemma is strong: without it, directory assistance makes Otto believe every listed number; with it, the organism's endorsement is the final authority. The memory comparisons are moderate: the internal side is cited research, the external side is thought experiment, and no experiment on an external store is run or cited. The step from "different fine-grained kinds" to "no useful coarse kind" is a challenge plus conservatism. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-540](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-540.md) | BCI software can be a body part, server not | Register (2025), [LIT-138](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-138.md), read in full in [NOTE-151](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-151.md). An argument from cases. It assumes that BCIs can be body parts and that no part of a person may be owned by another, and uses depth to reconcile the user's unqualified bodily ownership with the operator's property in the server. The two moral principles are its operative premises, and it says they do not depend on the real-definition ontology, which only explains them. The threshold for "high-level" is context-sensitive and unfixed, and the step that software and server are distinct coinciding objects is hedged. The conflict over servers is narrowed, not dissolved. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-549](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-549.md) | Groups with same members can still be two | Ritchie (2013, online 2012), [LIT-479](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-479.md), read in [NOTE-390](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-390.md), with its 2018 sequel [LIT-486](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-486.md) ([NOTE-389](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-389.md)). Six criteria for a theory of groups, each defended by one example, rule out non-singular pluralities, Sider's fusions, Burge's aggregates and Effingham's sets; the decisive one is Coincidence. Groups as realized structures meet all six. The refutations are strong given the criteria; the criteria rest on single cases, and the positive view is a four-page sketch with no persistence conditions. It says nothing about agency or minds. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-582](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-582.md) | Coupling alone doesn't make cognition extended | Adams & Aizawa (2001), [LIT-438](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-438.md), read in [NOTE-368](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-368.md), and their reply to Clark (2010, read from a draft), [LIT-455](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-455.md), read in [NOTE-380](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-380.md). A thermostat's bimetallic strip, the kidney's filtration and a nerve at a neuromuscular junction are each coupled to more than themselves, and their processes do not extend. The 2010 text names the inference the "coupling-constitution fallacy". The point is that coupling does not entail parthood. It is not shown that coupling never accompanies parthood, nor that the extended-mind authors relied on coupling alone. | Active |
| [THEORY-583](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-583.md) | Living systems are many nested agents | Levin (2019), [LIT-439](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-439.md), a hypothesis-and-theory essay read in full in [NOTE-341](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-341.md). A definition of the Self as a goal-pursuing collective, tied to a mechanism, gap-junctional coupling, from cited experiments on patterning and cancer. It has no model, no measurement of the light cone and no new data. Its goals are cybernetic set points, so any homeostat is a Self. Its Self is an agent and an individual, not a subject. The sentence against IIT's single Self is a bracket, and the closing remarks on experience are labelled speculation. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-585](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-585.md) v3 | Topos pull-backs fail for tensor composites | Döring & Isham, paper IV (2007/8), [LIT-310](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-310.md) ([NOTE-285](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-285.md)), restated in [LIT-378](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-378.md) §§11–13 ([NOTE-326](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-326.md)). The rules are "partly experimental", and the trivial-system rule contradicts the series' own definition of contexts. | Active |
| [THEORY-589](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-589.md) | No mereological principle is merely definitional | Varzi, SEP "Mereology", [LIT-124](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-124.md), read in full in [NOTE-163](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-163.md). The entry's verdict, reached by surveying counterexample families: Antisymmetry "can hardly be regarded as constitutive", and most ordinary-language objections to Reflexivity and Transitivity equivocate, leaving the metaphysical ones. It is the author's informal argument, and he is a known extensionalist who gives that side the last word on extensionality. Its headline that "all composition principles turn out to be controversial" is stronger than its own verdict that bounds for overlapping things are "rather uncontroversial". It corrects the record's earlier summary, which called the partial-order core uncontroversial. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-591](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-591.md) | Cognition is contingently bound to the brain | Adams & Aizawa (2001), [LIT-438](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-438.md), read in [NOTE-368](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-368.md), restated against Clark in 2010, [LIT-455](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-455.md), read in [NOTE-380](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-380.md) from a draft. | [THEORY-622](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-622.md) | Wholes of separate bodies are fiat objects | Smith & Varzi (2000), [LIT-1024](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1024.md), read in full in [NOTE-721](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-721.md). A typology with a formal sketch: ordinary closure topology for bona fide boundaries, and a Brentanian theory of coinciding boundaries for fiat ones, which are parts of what they bound. The test is whether a discontinuity is there, not who or what made it. The theory is spatial, synchronic and pitched at the common-sense level; it has no models or consistency result, and the typology is stipulated by examples. It does not map onto the record's produced/imposed distinction, and it classifies the record's combined forms as fiat without choosing among them. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-644](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-644.md) | Panpsychism's combination problems stay unsolved | Chalmers (2016/2017), [LIT-395](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-395.md), read in full in [NOTE-358](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-358.md) from the April 2015 draft. A map of the problem, not a solution or an impossibility proof, and the author says so. The dilemma is argued case by case; the strongest arguments against constitutive panpsychism, subject-summing and structural mismatch, rest on conceivability premises and on a structure-preservation principle called plausible, not shown. The verdicts on which responses are most promising are judgements of promise. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1287](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1287.md) | Mechanist experiments don't fix boundaries | Craver and Bechtel (2007), [LIT-1928](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1928.md), pp. 553–554, read in [NOTE-1491](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1491.md). The four kinds of interlevel experiment "share a form with Mill's methods" and are symmetrical. A lesion deficit is "only prima facie" evidence of componency, since a part "not interactively integrated" may be a background condition (n. 10). "Integrated" is never defined, and nothing in the four experiments tests where the system's edge is. That leaves the mechanism's boundary to be fixed some other way. | Active |
| [THEORY-1288](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1288.md) | Mutual manipulability is unsatisfiable | Baumgartner & Gebharter (2016), [LIT-1934](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1934.md), pp. 10–13, 18–20, and Baumgartner & Casini (2017), [LIT-1939](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1939.md), pp. 6–11; restated by Baumgartner, Casini & Krickel (2020) as Systematic Fat-Handedness. Active as a conditional: valid on supervenience and non-causal constitution, and checked step by step. It does not say that constitution cannot be known, only that no finite set of manipulations of whole and part shows it; and it is about simultaneous whole–part dependence, not about a diachronic cause inside a system, which can be intervened on surgically. | Active |
| [THEORY-1291](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1291.md) | Interlevel causes are mediated by constitution | Craver and Bechtel (2007), [LIT-1928](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1928.md), read in [NOTE-1491](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1491.md). Parts and wholes are not distinct events. So, given transmission, distinctness or asymmetry views of causation, they cannot be cause and effect, and the symmetry of interlevel experiments is explained by constitution. The six worked cases translate. The account says nothing about whether a feedback loop crossing the mechanism's boundary changes the analysis, and its generality is assumed. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1293](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1293.md) | One intervention shows constituency, given levels | Baumgartner, Casini & Krickel (2020), [LIT-1924](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1924.md), §§3–4, read in [NOTE-1494](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1494.md). | [THEORY-1294](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1294.md) | Constitution is inferred only abductively | Baumgartner & Casini (2017), [LIT-1939](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1939.md), §§4–5, their No De-Coupling account, developing the fat-handedness criterion of Baumgartner & Gebharter (2016), [LIT-1934](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1934.md), pp. 20–22. | [THEORY-1650](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1650.md) | Mereology fit to a norm can't support it | Mereological implications of the ethics of pregnancy (Dranseika, J Med Ethics 2026), read in [NOTE-1751](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1751.md) (Read), standing in for [LIT-2409](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2409.md). | [THEORY-1666](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1666.md) | Norms may break ties among pregnancy ontologies | Żuradzki (2026), Ethics-first metaphysics: normative considerations as evidence for ontological commitments, read in [NOTE-1744](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1744.md) (Read). Żuradzki accepts Devanesan's thesis that no ontology of pregnancy entails an ethical conclusion but that each constrains which analogies can support one, and argues that the relation is closer: where biological evidence underdetermines competing ontologies, considered normative judgments may themselves count as evidence for choosing between them.
